text:
Grade 4 students lead mathematics MCA participation at Salem Hills Elementary for 2024-25
T. A. Huey
Fourth-grade students at Salem Hills Elementaryearned the highest participation rate in the mathematics segment of the 2024-25 MCA, based on details from the Minnesota Department of Education.
There were 134 students from Salem Hills Elementary who completed the mathematics portion, with 47 of those students enrolled in grade 4.
According to the standards of the assessment, 45% of the fourth-grade participants achieved proficiency in mathematics.
The MCA and the Alternate Minnesota Comprehensive Assessment (Alt MCA) serve as the statewide measurements for student performance with respect to Minnesota’s academic standards, helping to fulfill both state and federal reporting requirements. These standardized assessments evaluate math, reading, and science, with subjects varying by grade. Most students are administered the MCA, while those qualifying for special education and meeting certain criteria may take the Alt MCA as an alternative.
Statewide performance in the MCA assessments has fallen since before the pandemic, as stated in data from Minnesota's Report Card. In mathematics, proficiency saw a decline of over 7% since 2019, and reading scores dropped by nearly 5% over the same time frame.
| Grade | # of Students Tested | Proficiency in mathematics |
|---|---|---|
| 3rd | 46 | 50% |
| 4th | 47 | 45% |
| 5th | 41 | 51% |
Information in this article was obtained from the Minnesota Department of Education. The source data can be found here.
